scope: Frozen n70 bilingual lesson text and zero exercises only
scriptBoundary: Structural/hash checks only; these scientific judgments record the independent reviewer's reading, not a computed scientific proof.

checks.assessment: Examples and spherical-mirror scope retained. Modern prose describes possible larger/smaller images rather than making unequal size an exceptionless law; the plane-mirror positional rule is not a universal curved-mirror rule.
Spherical reflecting surface and source point O retained; modern center-of-curvature terminology is explicitly separated from the source's optical-center term and from thin-lens usage.
Vertex P and axes through curvature center retain the source geometry and OP/OK notation.
Principal axis OP, symmetry-axis role and remaining secondary axes retain the source distinction; source introductory sentence is merged without losing its role.
Inner reflecting surface is concave and outer reflecting surface convex in both languages.
The optical-disk sequence and reversed middle ray are retained; side-ray meeting is explicitly approximate and linked to the footnote.
The principal-focus claim is correctly scoped to a concave mirror and paraxial rays; the labeled real-focus clarification uses actual reflected rays in front of the mirror.
First footnote preserves small ray height relative to sphere radius; modern spherical-aberration explanation prevents arbitrary-aperture exact-focus claims.
Secondary-axis beam, equal-distance approximation, focal surface and small-angle perpendicular focal-plane approximation are preserved with narrow-beam/aberration qualifications.

Focus-first staging, divergent rays toward the mirror and the luminous-point construction are preserved; reverse parallel-beam conclusion remains paraxial and is not confused with exact reversibility itself.
Real/virtual image outcomes are correctly tied to moving the luminous point beyond/inside the focus; real rays versus backward extensions and front/behind locations are distinguished.
Second footnote retains small incident angles relative to the principal axis; point imaging is not made an all-direction/all-aperture guarantee.
Convex reflected rays diverge and backward extensions meet at a virtual focus behind the mirror in the paraxial model; screen and actual-ray distinctions are clearly labeled modern clarification.

Focal length definition and source F symbol shared with focal-point label are preserved; modern vertex-to-focus measurement and need for a separate signed convention prevent curvature-center or point/length confusion.
